$comment: DERIVED, not verbatim. Written by this library from the prose of the W3C Recommendation Verifiable Credential Data Integrity 1.0 (REC-vc-data-integrity-20250515), which prints no JSON Schema, CDDL or ABNF of its own (README.md gives the search). Source .cache/w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0.bin, sha256 ba5c4baf13fe3bab3ebd95ab6650d6fe83720e254b383bb444b4fbbae7bcf4fe; quotations are cut from its rendering .cache/w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0.txt, sha256 2b7725f80e138ef943eff25050eee6a62f8887762ca9e1e03867c55ea5647beb, and cite its line numbers (L). LEVELS: the root and every anchor not ending in -should state MUST and MUST NOT rules, so a failure there is non-conformance; an anchor ending in -should adds SHOULD statements and includes the root by reference, so a failure there is a warning. MAY statements are never constraints: a leniency a MAY grants has its own anchor, named for the leniency. A constraint marked INFERRED is a reading this library made, not a statement of the source; one marked OUTSIDE-SOURCE comes from a document the source names and is not this source's. Rule ids (P-nn, S-nn, V-nn, E-nn, O-nn, M-nn) are those of rules.derived.yaml. INSTANCE: a secured data document, a JSON object that carries a proof (sections 2.1, 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 4). ROOT = MUST: a proof property whose value is one proof object or a non-empty array of them (an unordered set), each valid under proof.derived. ANCHORS: #single-proof (the document Verify Proof, 4.4, accepts), #proof-set-or-chain (the array form Verify Proof Sets and Chains, 4.5, accepts), #proof-chain-shape (the shape of section 2.1.2), #processable (every proof has verificationMethod), #context-should (SHOULD: an @context that carries the Data Integrity terms). The referential rules of a chain (previousProof names a proof of the same document) are cross-field rules X-01 to X-03 in rules.derived.yaml and are tested in check-schemas.derived.py; a JSON Schema cannot state them.
title: A secured data document (DERIVED)

proof.$comment: S-01 w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0002: “When expressing a data integrity proof on an object, a proof property MUST be used.” (L203) w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0003: “If present, its value MUST be either a single object, or an unordered set of objects, expressed using the properties below:” (L203) A set is an array. Non-empty: INFERRED from the definition “A secured data document is a map that contains one or more proof values.” (L531) (no keyword). An object is not an array and an array is not an object, so exactly one branch can hold.

@context.$comment: S-02 w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0032: SHOULD, #context-should. w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0033: a document that is not JSON-LD may omit it, and then w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0034: “However, if an @context declaration is not included, extensions (such as the addition of new properties) related to this specification or corresponding cryptosuites MUST NOT be made.” (L446) Not decidable from the document alone (what counts as an extension depends on the contexts), so no keyword states it.

single.$comment: ANCHOR #single-proof. The document Verify Proof (4.4) accepts: w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0066 “If either securedDocument is not a map or securedDocument.proof is not a map, an error MUST be raised and SHOULD convey an error type of PARSING_ERROR.” (L601)

set.$comment: ANCHOR #proof-set-or-chain. The document Verify Proof Sets and Chains (4.5) accepts: “In a proof set or proof chain, a secured data document has a proof attribute which contains a list of proofs (allProofs).” (L618)

chain.$comment: ANCHOR #proof-chain-shape. INFERRED reading of a sentence with no keyword: “A proof chain, where proof order needs to be preserved, is expressed by providing at least one proof with an id, such as a UUID [RFC9562], and another proof with a previousProof value that identifies the previous proof.” (L333) At least one proof has an id and a different proof has a previousProof. That the value names that id is X-01.

processable.$comment: ANCHOR #processable. Every proof has verificationMethod (P-19; README T-01).

contextShould.$comment: ANCHOR #context-should. SHOULD level. S-03 w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0032: “implementations SHOULD inject or append an @context property with a value of https://w3id.org/security/data-integrity/v2 or one or more contexts with at least the same declarations” (L445) The check holds the two contexts the source names, the Data Integrity v2 context and the Verifiable Credential Data Model v2.0 context; it cannot decide whether another context has at least the same declarations, so a document with such a context is flagged here and is not necessarily wrong.
